newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila grains importers waiting for price dips.
newsitem.headline: Manila grains importers waiting for price dips.

text.p: Philippine grain importers, sidelined by the fall of the peso and high U.S. wheat and corn prices this week, are waiting for prices to soften being going back to the market, traders said.
"There could be some activity next week if prices dip to better levels, " said an executive in a local flour mill.
Executives of local mills said they were hoping U.S. wheat prices would drop next week after Pakistan and Egypt satisfy their requirements of a total 500,000 tonnes wheat.
"Hopefully prices will be better after both countries finalise their orders," another executive said.
Manila grains buyers said they did not plan to buy wheat, corn and soybean for next year even though the El Nino weather phenomenon was expected to hit crops in Asia-Pacific countries.
"Not many people can buy because of the lack of silos," said an executive in a local flour mill.
Philippine Association of Hog Raisers Inc president Soledad Agbayani said she expected a rise in the prices of corn, wheat and soybean due to El Nino.
"Corn-producing countries, including the United States, would hoard for their own needs," she said.

Rolando Dy, executive director of the Center for Food and Agribusiness of the University of Asia and the Pacific, recommended that the country make early bookings for the import of about 950,000 tonnes for delivery in the first half of 1998.
Dy said he expected Philippine rice harvests to drop by 15 percent to 2.7 million tonnes in the first half of 1998 from 3.2 million in the first half of 1997.
